event.title: Physics Show (September 18)
event.description:
Thought you needed an expensive airplane ticket to be in a cloud?


Just come to the Hawking Auditorium on the Texas A&M campus. Clouds, lightning, and magic bubbles! Solid air and liquid oxygen! Racquetballs fragile like glass and bananas as rigid as hammers! Levitating trains and floating toilet paper! All this and much more in the Hawking Auditorium. And none of it is magic, it’s Physics!

 

And you know what the best part is? Physics experiments that YOU can do at HOME! Want to start every morning with a physics experiment? Come to the Physics Show and get the ideas.

 

Ages: All

 

Cost: Free

 

More information can be found here.

event.title: 150th Celebration Opening Ceremony
event.description:
In 2026, Texas A&M University invites Aggies everywhere to stand together to celebrate 150 years as a force for good in Texas, the nation and beyond. Join us for the 150th Celebration Opening Ceremony.

Gather at the steps of the Jack K. Williams Administration Building for the official kickoff of the sesquicentennial celebration. The 150th anniversary of our university will be commemorated with an official proclamation and remarks by leadership, along with student performances celebrating Texas A&M’s rich history and traditions.

The event is open to the public with a reception to follow.

event.title: Garden Exploration Days (October 12 - 13)
event.description:
Dig into the exciting world of plants, gardening, and nature at Garden Exploration Days! Hosted by the Junior Master Gardener Program and The Gardens at Texas A&M University, this hands-on day camp series is designed for students entering 2nd–5th grade and encourages curiosity, discovery, and a love for the natural world through engaging, experiential learning.

Each Garden Exploration Day features a unique theme, giving campers the opportunity to discover a different aspect of gardening and environmental science. Using activities from the JMG curriculum, participants will investigate plant growth, soils, pollinators, insects, ecosystems, and sustainable gardening practices through interactive experiences.

Ages: 6-10

Cost: $75 per day or $140 if you register for both – includes all materials and supplies for lessons and activities

Registration and more information can be found here.

event.title: Aggieland Saturday by the Sea
event.description:
Our free, all-access open house, Aggieland Saturday by the Sea, is an immersive event, offering you a 360º introduction to Texas A&M’s island campus, including: 

 

  • Information sessions about the admissions process, financial aid and student life; 
  • An intro to the Texas A&M Maritime Academy, the Corps of Cadets, professional maritime license options and programs;
  • Visit research labs and training simulators, and tour the new 524-foot state-of-the-art training vessel, Lone Star State; 
  • Experience fun Aggie traditions and hospitality with our student organizations;
  • And much more!

event.title: Chemistry Open House & Science Exploration
event.description:
The Chemistry Open House features the popular Chemistry Road Show, guided lab tours, hands-on and computer activities, door prizes and science goodie bags. The Chemistry Road Show is recommended for all ages and includes demonstrations of popular science. Participants include the Departments of Atmospheric Sciences, Biology, Physics and Astronomy and more, along with students from the College of Engineering and SACNAS.

Activities

  • Chemistry Road Show featuring chemical wonders, super cold materials and other exciting demonstrations
  • Lab tours for both general chemistry and organic chemistry spaces
  • Hands-on and polymer and computer activities
  • Many other fascinating demonstrations

Food

  • A Lunch Buffet is available at Sbisa Dining Hall.
  • See Dining Services - Places to Eat web site for more options.

Ages: All

Cost: Free

More information can be found here.

Meeting once a week, participants will explore the fascinating sciences of gardening, horticulture, botany, and entomology through interactive lessons, creative projects, outdoor investigations, and garden-based activities.

 

Ages: 6-9

 

Cost: $80

 

Registration and more information can be found here.

Through hands-on activities, garden exploration, stories, and interactive lessons from the Junior Master Gardener curriculum, little gardeners will discover the amazing world of plants—from roots and stems to flowers and fruits—and learn what gardens need to thrive!

 

Ages: 3-5

 

Cost: $45

 

Registration and more information can be found here.

event.title: Veterinary Science Camp Middle School (November 3 - 4)
event.description:
Join the Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Veterinary Science Program (VSCP) for a hands-on Middle School Day Camp hosted by Fossil Rim Wildlife Center in Glen Rose, Texas, on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

This event is designed for middle school students who are interested in animals, veterinary science, wildlife, conservation, and careers working with animals.

Students will spend the day exploring Fossil Rim Wildlife Center and participating in engaging, hands-on learning experiences. The day will include a guided tour of Fossil Rim, followed by activities focused on animal husbandry, nutrition, enrichment, veterinary practices, and conservation.

Students will have the opportunity to learn how professionals care for wildlife while gaining exposure to veterinary science and animal-related careers.

 

Ages: 11-14

 

Cost: $135

 

More information and registration can be found here.

event.title: The Aggie Family Parade
event.description:
In 2026, Texas A&M University invites Aggies everywhere to stand together to celebrate 150 years as a force for good in Texas, the nation and beyond. Join us during the Spirit of 150 Week.

For the first time in university history, Family Weekend will feature a celebratory parade through campus with student organizations, college floats, community marching bands and more. The local community, former students, faculty, staff and students are invited to watch this historic procession led by the Fightin’ Texas Aggie Band and the Corps of Cadets.

event.title: 150th Celebration Closing Festival
event.description:
In 2026, Texas A&M University invites Aggies everywhere to stand together to celebrate 150 years as a force for good in Texas, the nation and beyond. Join us during the Spirit of 150 Week.

The official 150th anniversary celebration will conclude with an outdoor festival in and around Aggie Park, which is open to the public. The festival will feature carnival rides, games, live music, food vendors and Aggie product and apparel vendors. Kyle Field will be open for photo opportunities.
